A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMARTER study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and cross-model experiments, style analyses, and human preferences for explanations of 342 samples (Figures 3–5 and Table 3).

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated baselines, repeated-seed comparisons, and explanation-consistency results (Tables 1, 3, 5 and 6).

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same models, HateCOT pretraining, label-conditioned preference optimization, and cross-model SFT/DPO refinement. The new NLI checks evaluate explanations rather than alter SMARTER's training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HateCOT and the same three English classification tasks: HateXplain, Latent Hate, and its fine-grained Implicit Hate subset. Added baseline comparisons and consistency analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-5-chat and Qwen-32B comparators under zero-shot and 16-shot prompting, plus off-the-shelf Llama and T5 comparisons (Tables 1 and 5). ModernBERT and the full-data Llama/T5 baselines already appeared in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include label-only off-the-shelf evaluation, commercial-model prompting with 16 examples per class, and GPT-4o-mini consistency judgments checked against author annotations. Definition consistency is evaluated only on explanations passing label consistency. Existing splits and training budgets persist; Table 1 also changes relative-F1 normalization.

E4.justification: v3 adds an off-the-shelf comparison to examine pretraining contributions and substantial analyses of explanation-label and explanation-definition consistency (Section 7). Appendix E and Figure 16 add contradiction patterns and failure examples. The earlier style, category-level and cross-model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting for 16-shot comparisons, with minima, maxima and ranges in Table 6. It also reports author–judge agreement using Cohen's kappa, 0.92 and 0.96. These additions do not establish repeated runs or uncertainty estimates for the retained SMARTER training results.

E6.justification: v3 adds off-the-shelf scores, external-model comparisons and consistency distributions. For example, GPT-4o-mini scores 0.50 on HateXplain under zero-shot prompting and 0.29 ± 0.10 under 16-shot prompting; label-consistency entailment ranges from 96.4% to 99.6%. Original classification, cross-model, style and per-class figure values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The defined relative score F1% changes mathematically: v1 Table 2 divides each DPO score by its corresponding full-data model's score, whereas v3 Table 1 normalizes all scores by the dataset's best score. This is a limited definition change; no new theorem, proof or theoretical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The two-stage data-efficiency contribution remains, but v3 adds prominent claims of outperforming commercial alternatives and providing deterministic, cheaper production deployment (Introduction and Section 8). This substantially expands the practical claims beyond v1's few-shot classification and explanation-refinement claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets cross-model refinement as potentially trading classification gains for explanation inconsistency. Appendix E discusses architecture-dependent error patterns and proposes NLI monitoring for deployment. The limitations also newly identify random sampling as a potential constraint and suggest more strategic selection.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds temperature, token limits, vLLM usage, an exact Qwen checkpoint and GPT-5 access date. New prompt templates and the previously omitted Incitement definition improve documentation. The repository address changes, while explicit GPT-3.5-Turbo seed attribution disappears; hardware, LoRA settings and tuning tables remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially reframes alignment positioning from sycophancy and debiasing toward computationally expensive RL versus inexpensive synthetic-data self-improvement, adding Self-Refine and Self-Instruct. v3 also introduces explanation-evaluation literature and explicitly contrasts its multiclass setting with earlier moderation research.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites and condenses related work, setup descriptions and discussion. Cross-model methodology, classification results and style analysis receive separate subsections, and explanation consistency receives a dedicated section and appendix. These changes reorganize the narrative beyond simply inserting new results.

P2.justification: The compact full-data comparison becomes a broad, full-width comparison table. Dataset details, the classification prompt and the style plot move to appendices; new consistency, baseline and variability tables and contradiction examples are added. v3 Figure 2 redisplays an existing example rather than introducing a new case.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through broader comparisons, seed-variation reporting and consistency checks validated against author annotations. These improve on v1's accuracy, style and preference evidence. The gain is limited because the pretraining comparison changes multiple conditions, while stronger claims of cheaper production deployment lack measured cost comparisons. The core SMARTER results remain unchanged.
